# pgmq

> Official Python client for [PGMQ](https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq) (Postgres Message Queue). One public API across four backends.

- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pgmq/
- Docs: https://pgmq.github.io/pgmq-py/
- Source: https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq-py
- Extension: https://github.com/pgmq/pgmq
- Maintainer map for agents that change this repo: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)

Python 3.10+. License Apache-2.0. Package version is `1.1.2`.

## Install

```bash
pip install pgmq
pip install pgmq[async]                 # asyncpg
pip install pgmq[sqlalchemy]            # SQLAlchemy sync
pip install pgmq[sqlalchemy-async]      # SQLAlchemy async + asyncpg
```

## Clients (identical public methods)

| Import | Backend | Extra | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|-------|
| `from pgmq import PGMQueue` | psycopg (sync) | default | Backward-compat default |
| `from pgmq import SyncPGMQueue` | psycopg (sync) | default | Same class as `PGMQueue` |
| `from pgmq import AsyncPGMQueue` | asyncpg | `[async]` | Call `await queue.init()` first |
| `from pgmq import SQLAlchemyPGMQueue` | SQLAlchemy Engine | `[sqlalchemy]` | |
| `from pgmq import SQLAlchemyAsyncPGMQueue` | SQLAlchemy AsyncEngine | `[sqlalchemy-async]` | Call `await queue.init()` first |

Optional clients are `None` when the extra is not installed.

## Capacity

Queue management: `create_queue`, `create_partitioned_queue`, `drop_queue`, `list_queues`, `validate_queue_name`

Send: `send`, `send_batch`, `send_topic`, `send_batch_topic` (headers, delay as seconds or `datetime`; `tz` is a `delay` alias)

Topic routing: `bind_topic`, `unbind_topic`, `list_topic_bindings`, `test_routing`

Read: `read`, `read_batch`, `read_with_poll`, `read_grouped`, `read_grouped_with_poll`, `read_grouped_rr`, `read_grouped_rr_with_poll` (optional JSONB `conditional` on recent extension versions)

Pop / delete / archive: `pop`, `delete`, `delete_batch`, `archive`, `archive_batch`, `purge`

Other: `set_vt`, `metrics`, `metrics_all`, `enable_notify`, `disable_notify`, `update_notify`, `list_notify_throttles`, FIFO index helpers, archive partition helpers

Dataclasses: `Message`, `QueueRecord`, `QueueMetrics`, `TopicBinding`, `RoutingResult`, `NotificationThrottle`

Transactions: pass `conn=` to compose operations, or use `transaction` / `async_transaction` / `sqlalchemy_transaction` / `sqlalchemy_async_transaction`

## Postgres setup

Prefer the official extension:

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION pgmq;
```

Docker image: `ghcr.io/pgmq/pg18-pgmq:latest`

SQL-only install (hosted Postgres that cannot load extensions):

```python
from pgmq import install_pgmq_from_sql, PGMQueue

install_pgmq_from_sql(host="localhost", port="5432", username="postgres", password="postgres", database="postgres")
queue = PGMQueue(init_extension=False, host="localhost", port="5432", username="postgres", password="postgres", database="postgres")
```

SQL-only install does **not** support extension versioning or `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE`. It applies a pinned snapshot of `pgmq.sql`. Re-running it on an existing `pgmq` schema is not supported. Prefer `CREATE EXTENSION pgmq` when the host allows extensions.

## Configuration

`PGMQConfig` reads `PG_HOST`, `PG_PORT`, `PG_DATABASE`, `PG_USERNAME`, `PG_PASSWORD`, `DATABASE_URL`, and `PG_INIT_EXTENSION`. Pass a DSN or field kwargs. Clients use the rebuilt `dsn` / `async_dsn`, not the raw string.

Set `init_extension=False` (or `PG_INIT_EXTENSION=false`) after a SQL-only install so the client does not run `CREATE EXTENSION`.

## Compatibility notes

- `list_queues()` returns `list[QueueRecord]`, not `list[str]`.
- `read_batch()` is `read(..., qty=batch_size)`.
- `AsyncPGMQueue` and `SQLAlchemyAsyncPGMQueue` require `await init()` before any operation.
- Newer features (topic routing, conditional reads, validation helpers, partitioning, advanced notify) need a recent PGMQ extension. They are not available after every SQL-only snapshot.
